```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Friedrich 2014 analysed a 12-week phase II study of evacetrapib, a
cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibitor, with three sequentially
fitted models: a population PK model, and two exposure-response models for the
percent change from baseline in HDL-C and LDL-C that take each patient's
steady-state evacetrapib AUC from the PK model as their exposure. The three are
packaged as three model files:

* `Friedrich_2014_evacetrapib` -- population PK.
* `Friedrich_2014_evacetrapib_hdl` -- HDL-C percent change (Eq. 1).
* `Friedrich_2014_evacetrapib_ldl` -- LDL-C percent change (Eqs. 2 and 3).

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Friedrich_2014_evacetrapib"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/psp.2013.70> (open access; the
  supplementary data hold the authors' NONMEM code and final estimates for all
  three models).

```{r models}
mod_pk <- readModelDb("Friedrich_2014_evacetrapib")
mod_hdl <- readModelDb("Friedrich_2014_evacetrapib_hdl")
mod_ldl <- readModelDb("Friedrich_2014_evacetrapib_ldl")
```

# Population

The study randomised 398 adults with hypercholesterolemia or low HDL-C
(triglycerides below 400 mg/dL after a lipid washout and dietary lead-in) to
12 weeks of placebo; evacetrapib 30, 100 or 500 mg once daily; atorvastatin
20 mg, simvastatin 40 mg or rosuvastatin 10 mg once daily; or each statin with
evacetrapib 100 mg once daily (about 40 per arm). 56.0% were female and 92.9%
white; age was 28-83 years (mean 58.3) and body weight 44-164 kg (mean 83.6).
Mean baseline LDL-C, HDL-C and triglycerides were 144.3, 55.1 and 139.8 mg/dL
(Results). The PK model used 1,629 concentrations from 226 patients, the HDL-C
model 1,882 observations from 391 patients and the LDL-C model 1,469
observations from 388 patients. The same information is available
programmatically, e.g. `rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Friedrich_2014_evacetrapib"))$population`.

# Source trace

Every value below is the final estimate printed in the authors' NONMEM output
(Supplementary Data) and agrees with the corresponding row of Tables 1-3.

| Model | Parameter / equation | Value | Source location |
|-------|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| PK | `lka` | log(0.3) (held constant) | Table 1; NONMEM THETA(1) |
| PK | `lcl` | log(15.3) L/h | Table 1; THETA(2) |
| PK | `lvc` | log(228) L | Table 1; THETA(3) |
| PK | `lq` | log(9.79) L/h | Table 1; THETA(4) |
| PK | `lvp` | log(827) L | Table 1; THETA(5) |
| PK | `e_dose_cl` | 0.00105 /mg | Table 1 and footnote c; THETA(6) |
| PK | `e_crcl_cl` | 0.00198 /(mL/min), centred at 91.28 | Table 1 and footnote c; THETA(7) |
| PK | `etalcl + etalvc` | 0.144, 0.225, 0.426 | NONMEM $OMEGA BLOCK(2); Table 1 (39.4%, 50.2%, 72.9%) |
| PK | `etalq` | 1.04 | NONMEM OMEGA(4); Table 1 (135.2%) |
| PK | `propSd` | 0.3302 = sqrt(0.109) | NONMEM SIGMA; Table 1 (33%) |
| PK | CL/F equation | `15.3 * (1 + 0.00105 * DOSE) * (1 + 0.00198 * (CGCL - 91.28))` | Table 1 footnote c; NONMEM $PK |
| PK | `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` (ng/mL) | n/a | NONMEM $PK `S2 = V2/1000` |
| HDL | `emax` | 177 % | Table 2; THETA(1) |
| HDL | `lauc50` | 8.59 (exp = 5,379 ng*h/mL) | NONMEM THETA(2); Table 2 (5,380) |
| HDL | `e_hdlc_lauc50` | 0.00317 /(mg/dL), centred at 52.2 | Table 2; THETA(7); NONMEM $PRED |
| HDL | `lhill` | log(1) (held constant) | NONMEM THETA(3); Results |
| HDL | `plac` | 0 (held constant) | Table 2; THETA(4) |
| HDL | `e_conmed_statin_hdl` | 0 (held constant) | NONMEM THETA(6); Results |
| HDL | `lkhdl` | log(0.00684) /h | Table 2; THETA(5) |
| HDL | `etaemax`, `etalkhdl`, `etaplac` | 3680, 0.281, 59.7 | NONMEM $OMEGA; Table 2 (34.3%, 57%, 7.7) |
| HDL | `addSd` | 14.18 = sqrt(201) | NONMEM SIGMA; Table 2 (14.2) |
| HDL | `hdlcfb = (PLAC + STAT * I + Emax * AUC / (EAUC50 + AUC)) * (1 - exp(-K * time))` | n/a | Eqs. 1 and 4; NONMEM $PRED |
| LDL | `emax` | -44.1 % | Table 3; THETA(1) |
| LDL | `lauc50` | 8.35 (exp = 4,230 ng*h/mL) | NONMEM THETA(2); Table 3 (4,230) |
| LDL | `e_apoa1_emax` | -0.989, reference 153 mg/dL | Table 3 and footnote d; THETA(5) |
| LDL | `plac` | 0 (held constant) | Table 3; NONMEM TVPLAC |
| LDL | `e_ldlc_plac` | -0.119, centred at 146.56 mg/dL | Table 3 and footnote e; THETA(6); NONMEM $PRED |
| LDL | `e_trig_plac` | 1.87, reference 120.01 mg/dL | Table 3 and footnote e; THETA(7); NONMEM $PRED |
| LDL | `e_conmed_statin_ldl` | -38.7 % | Table 3; THETA(3) |
| LDL | `e_inter` | -0.997 | Table 3; THETA(4) |
| LDL | `etaplac` | 140 | NONMEM OMEGA(1); Table 3 (11.8) |
| LDL | `addSd` | 11.31 = sqrt(128) | NONMEM SIGMA; Table 3 (11.3) |
| LDL | `ldlcfb = PLAC + STAT * I_ST + LY * (1 - I_COMB) + INTER * I_COMB * 100 * (1 - (1 + STAT/100) * (1 + LY/100))` | n/a | Eqs. 2 and 3; NONMEM $PRED |

# Checks against statements in the paper

Several results in the paper are deterministic functions of the typical-value
model and can be checked exactly.

```{r deterministic-checks}
# CL/F at the median CGCL for each dose level, and the CGCL effect.
cl_typ <- function(dose, crcl) 15.3 * (1 + 0.00105 * dose) * (1 + 0.00198 * (crcl - 91.28))
cl_by_dose <- tibble(
  dose = c(30, 100, 500),
  cl_model = cl_typ(dose, 91.28),
  cl_text = c(13.1, 17.0, 25.4)
)
crcl_ratio <- cl_typ(100, 50) / cl_typ(100, 100)

# HDL-C: fraction of Emax reached at the geometric-mean AUC of each dose group
# (Discussion: "~30, 50, and 80% of the maximal effect").
auc_gm <- c(2300, 5900, 19700)
frac_emax <- auc_gm / (exp(8.59) + auc_gm)

hdl_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_hdl)
ldl_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ldl)

# Typical-value solves of several rows at once: rxode2 warns that a
# multi-subject solve has no omega, which is the intent here.
solve_typical <- function(mod, d) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod, d),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

hdl_at <- function(auc, hdlc, time = 12 * 7 * 24) {
  d <- data.frame(
    id = seq_along(auc), time = time, AUC_EVACETRAPIB = auc,
    HDLC = hdlc, CONMED_STATIN = 0
  )
  solve_typical(hdl_typ, d)$hdlcfb
}

# Discussion: an AUC giving +110% at baseline HDL-C 55 mg/dL gives +127% at
# 40 mg/dL (the DEFINE study's mean baseline).
auc_110 <- uniroot(function(a) hdl_at(a, 55) - 110, c(1000, 50000))$root
hdl_define <- hdl_at(auc_110, 40)

checks <- tibble(
  Claim = c(
    "CL/F 10% lower at CGCL 50 than 100 mL/min (Results)",
    "30 mg: fraction of HDL-C Emax ~30% (Discussion)",
    "100 mg: fraction of HDL-C Emax ~50% (Discussion)",
    "500 mg: fraction of HDL-C Emax ~80% (Discussion)",
    "+110% at HDL-C 55 mg/dL becomes +127% at 40 mg/dL (Discussion)"
  ),
  Paper = c(10, 30, 50, 80, 127),
  Model = c(100 * (1 - crcl_ratio), 100 * frac_emax, hdl_define)
)
knitr::kable(checks, digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  abs(checks$Model[1] - 10) < 1,
  all(abs(checks$Model[2:4] - c(30, 50, 80)) < 3),
  abs(hdl_define - 127) < 2
)
```

The CL/F values that the Results text quotes for the three dose levels (13.1,
17.0 and 25.4 L/h) are not what the Table 1 covariate equation gives at the
median CGCL:

```{r cl-by-dose}
cl_by_dose |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg)" = dose,
    "CL/F from Table 1 equation (L/h)" = cl_model,
    "CL/F quoted in Results (L/h)" = cl_text
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

The quoted values match the spread of the individual post hoc clearances by
dose group in Supplementary Figure S3 (medians read as about 12.4, 15.3 and
24.8 L/h), and they reproduce the published geometric-mean AUCs exactly
(1000 x 30 / 13.1 = 2,290; 1000 x 500 / 25.4 = 19,690 ng*h/mL), so they are
summaries of the individual estimates rather than the typical-value curve. The
linear dose term understates the curvature between 30 and 100 mg; the
simulated AUC at 30 mg is therefore lower than published (see the NCA
comparison below). The equation in Table 1 and the NONMEM code is used as
published.

# PK simulation

## Virtual cohort

Covariate distributions are assumptions (the paper gives the median CGCL but
no spread): CGCL is drawn log-normally around the 91.28 mL/min median with a
30% coefficient of variation and truncated to 30-200 mL/min. PK is not
affected by statin coadministration, so one PK cohort per evacetrapib dose
level is simulated (100 patients each), plus a separate 100 mg cohort that
supplies AUCs for the evacetrapib + statin arm of the exposure-response
simulations.

```{r pk-cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20140101)
set.seed(20140101)

n_per_arm <- 100
pk_arms <- tibble(
  treatment = c("30 mg", "100 mg", "500 mg", "100 mg + statin"),
  dose = c(30, 100, 500, 100)
)
tau <- 24
n_dose <- 84
t_last_dose <- (n_dose - 1) * tau

make_pk_cohort <- function(arm, dose, id_offset) {
  crcl <- exp(rnorm(n_per_arm, log(91.28), 0.3))
  crcl <- pmin(pmax(crcl, 30), 200)
  subj <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_per_arm),
    treatment = arm, DOSE = dose, CRCL = crcl
  )
  doses <- subj |>
    mutate(time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ii = tau, addl = n_dose - 1)
  obs_times <- c(seq(0, 7 * 24, by = 6), seq(t_last_dose, t_last_dose + tau, by = 0.25))
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = 0, addl = 0)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, ii, addl, DOSE, CRCL, treatment)
}

pk_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pk_arms)), function(i) {
  make_pk_cohort(pk_arms$treatment[i], pk_arms$dose[i], (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(pk_events[pk_events$evid == 1, "id"]))
```

```{r pk-simulate}
pk_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = pk_events, keep = c("treatment", "DOSE"))
pk_sim <- as.data.frame(pk_sim)
```

## Concentration-time profiles

```{r pk-profiles, fig.height = 4}
pk_sim |>
  filter(time >= t_last_dose, treatment != "100 mg + statin") |>
  mutate(tad = time - t_last_dose) |>
  group_by(treatment, tad) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("30 mg", "100 mg", "500 mg"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the week-12 dose (h)", y = "Evacetrapib (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Median and 90% interval of simulated steady-state concentrations."
  )
```

## Steady-state AUC (PKNCA)

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- pk_sim |>
  filter(time >= t_last_dose, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

nca_dose <- pk_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, ii, addl, treatment) |>
  mutate(n = addl + 1) |>
  tidyr::uncount(n, .id = "k") |>
  mutate(time = time + (k - 1) * ii) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = t_last_dose, end = t_last_dose + tau,
  auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

The paper reports the geometric-mean AUC over the dosing interval at steady
state for each group (Results; Supplementary Figure S2).

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~auclast,
  "30 mg", 2300,
  "100 mg", 5900,
  "500 mg", 19700,
  "100 mg + statin", 5620
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (median) vs published (geometric mean) steady-state AUC over 24 h. * differs by >20%.")
```

The 100 mg + statin reference is the middle of the three published
combination-arm geometric means (5,500, 5,620 and 5,960 ng*h/mL for
atorvastatin, simvastatin and rosuvastatin). The 30 mg arm runs below the
published value because of the linear dose term discussed above.

The AUC over one dosing interval at steady state equals `1000 * DOSE / cl` for
the same simulated patient; this is the quantity the exposure-response models
take as `AUC_EVACETRAPIB`. The two agree to within trapezoidal error:

```{r auc-closed-form}
auc_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, treatment, auc_nca = PPORRES)
subj_pk <- pk_sim |>
  group_by(id, treatment) |>
  summarise(DOSE = first(DOSE), cl = first(cl), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(AUC_EVACETRAPIB = 1000 * DOSE / cl)
auc_chk <- inner_join(auc_nca, subj_pk, by = c("id", "treatment")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc_nca - AUC_EVACETRAPIB) / AUC_EVACETRAPIB)
stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_chk) == nrow(subj_pk),
  abs(median(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 3
)
summary(auc_chk$pct_diff)
```

```{r auc-boxplot, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Supplementary Figure S2 of Friedrich 2014: AUCtau,ss by group.
subj_pk |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = pk_arms$treatment)) |>
  ggplot(aes(treatment, AUC_EVACETRAPIB)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "AUCtau,ss (ng*h/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Supplementary Figure S2 of Friedrich 2014."
  )
```

# Exposure-response simulations

## Virtual cohort

Baseline lipids are drawn independently (an assumption; the paper does not
publish their spread or correlations): HDL-C log-normal with the 52.2 mg/dL
median and the 55.1 mg/dL mean implying a log-scale SD of 0.33; triglycerides
log-normal with the 120.01 mg/dL median and 139.8 mg/dL mean (log-scale SD
0.55), truncated below the 400 mg/dL entry limit; LDL-C normal around the
146.56 mg/dL median with an SD of 35 mg/dL; ApoA1 log-normal around the
153 mg/dL median with a log-scale SD of 0.18. Placebo and statin-only arms
have an AUC of 0. HDL-C and LDL-C are evaluated at the week 2, 4, 8 and 12
visits.

```{r pd-cohort}
pd_subj <- bind_rows(
  subj_pk |> select(id, treatment, AUC_EVACETRAPIB),
  tibble(id = 400L + seq_len(n_per_arm), treatment = "Placebo", AUC_EVACETRAPIB = 0),
  tibble(id = 500L + seq_len(n_per_arm), treatment = "Statin", AUC_EVACETRAPIB = 0)
)
n_pd <- nrow(pd_subj)
pd_subj <- pd_subj |>
  mutate(
    CONMED_STATIN = as.integer(treatment %in% c("Statin", "100 mg + statin")),
    HDLC = exp(rnorm(n_pd, log(52.2), 0.33)),
    TRIG = pmin(exp(rnorm(n_pd, log(120.01), 0.55)), 399),
    LDLC = pmax(rnorm(n_pd, 146.56, 35), 60),
    APOA1 = exp(rnorm(n_pd, log(153), 0.18))
  )
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(pd_subj$id))
visits <- c(2, 4, 8, 12) * 7 * 24
pd_events <- tidyr::crossing(pd_subj, time = visits) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L) |>
  arrange(id, time)
```

```{r pd-simulate}
hdl_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_hdl, events = pd_events, keep = "treatment"))
ldl_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ldl, events = pd_events, keep = "treatment"))
```

## Time course by arm

```{r figure-1, fig.height = 6}
# Compare with Figure 1 of Friedrich 2014 (observed mean percent change by
# monotherapy arm).
arm_levels <- c("Placebo", "30 mg", "100 mg", "500 mg", "Statin", "100 mg + statin")
pd_means <- bind_rows(
  hdl_sim |> group_by(treatment, time) |>
    summarise(mean = mean(hdlcfb), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(endpoint = "HDL-C"),
  ldl_sim |> group_by(treatment, time) |>
    summarise(mean = mean(ldlcfb), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(endpoint = "LDL-C")
) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = arm_levels), week = time / (7 * 24))

ggplot(pd_means, aes(week, mean, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Week", y = "Mean % change from baseline", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Simulated arm means; compare Figure 1 of Friedrich 2014."
  )
```

Week-12 arm means against the observed means read from Figure 1 (monotherapy
arms only; the paper does not plot the statin arms):

```{r week12-table}
fig1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~endpoint, ~observed,
  "Placebo", "HDL-C", -2,
  "30 mg", "HDL-C", 56,
  "100 mg", "HDL-C", 94,
  "500 mg", "HDL-C", 133,
  "Placebo", "LDL-C", 3,
  "30 mg", "LDL-C", -14,
  "100 mg", "LDL-C", -22,
  "500 mg", "LDL-C", -37
)
wk12 <- pd_means |>
  filter(week == 12) |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment)) |>
  inner_join(fig1, by = c("treatment", "endpoint"))
stopifnot(nrow(wk12) == nrow(fig1))
wk12 |>
  select(endpoint, treatment, mean, observed) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Endpoint" = endpoint, "Arm" = treatment,
    "Simulated mean (%)" = mean, "Figure 1 observed mean (%)" = observed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
# Robust envelope on arm means of 100 simulated patients: the largest gap is
# about 9 points (the 30 mg HDL-C arm, which inherits the low 30 mg AUC) and
# the 500 mg HDL-C arm mean has a Monte Carlo SE near 5 points. A
# mis-transcribed Emax, EAUC50 or unit moves an arm mean by tens of points.
stopifnot(all(abs(wk12$mean - wk12$observed) < 25))
```

## Figure 2: HDL-C response against baseline HDL-C

```{r figure-2, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 2 of Friedrich 2014: typical HDL-C % change at week 12 at
# an AUC of 9,500 ng*h/mL.
fig2 <- tibble(HDLC = seq(35, 65, by = 1)) |>
  mutate(hdlcfb = hdl_at(rep(9500, n()), HDLC))
fig2_digitised <- tibble(HDLC = c(35, 50, 65), paper = c(130, 114, 98))
fig2_chk <- inner_join(fig2, fig2_digitised, by = "HDLC")
stopifnot(nrow(fig2_chk) == 3, all(abs(fig2_chk$hdlcfb - fig2_chk$paper) < 3))
ggplot(fig2, aes(HDLC, hdlcfb)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig2_digitised, aes(y = paper), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "HDL-C at baseline (mg/dL)", y = "HDL-C % change from baseline at week 12",
    caption = "Line: model. Circles: read from Figure 2 of Friedrich 2014."
  )
```

## Figure 3: response against evacetrapib AUC

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 3 of Friedrich 2014 at median baseline covariates.
auc_grid <- seq(0, 30000, by = 500)
ldl_at <- function(auc) {
  d <- data.frame(
    id = seq_along(auc), time = 336, AUC_EVACETRAPIB = auc,
    APOA1 = 153, LDLC = 146.56, TRIG = 120.01, CONMED_STATIN = 0
  )
  solve_typical(ldl_typ, d)$ldlcfb
}
fig3 <- bind_rows(
  tibble(AUC = auc_grid, value = hdl_at(auc_grid, 52.2), endpoint = "HDL-C (week 12)"),
  tibble(AUC = auc_grid, value = ldl_at(auc_grid), endpoint = "LDL-C (steady state)")
)
fig3_digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~AUC, ~paper, ~endpoint,
  5000, 81, "HDL-C (week 12)",
  10000, 111, "HDL-C (week 12)",
  20000, 137, "HDL-C (week 12)",
  30000, 148, "HDL-C (week 12)",
  5000, -24, "LDL-C (steady state)",
  10000, -31, "LDL-C (steady state)",
  20000, -36.5, "LDL-C (steady state)",
  30000, -38.6, "LDL-C (steady state)"
)
fig3_chk <- inner_join(fig3, fig3_digitised, by = c("AUC", "endpoint"))
stopifnot(nrow(fig3_chk) == 8, all(abs(fig3_chk$value - fig3_chk$paper) < 5))
ggplot(fig3, aes(AUC, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig3_digitised, aes(y = paper), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Evacetrapib AUC (ng*h/mL)", y = "% change from baseline",
    caption = "Line: model at median covariates. Circles: read from Figure 3 of Friedrich 2014."
  )
```

## Statin interaction

With the estimated interaction coefficient of -0.997 the LDL-C reduction in
the combination arms is, to within 0.3%, the product of the two independent
fractional reductions, which is the paper's conclusion of pharmacologic
independence:

```{r statin-interaction}
d_int <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3, time = 336, AUC_EVACETRAPIB = c(0, 5900, 5900),
  APOA1 = 153, LDLC = 146.56, TRIG = 120.01, CONMED_STATIN = c(1, 0, 1)
)
ldl_int <- solve_typical(ldl_typ, d_int)$ldlcfb
independent <- 100 * ((1 + ldl_int[1] / 100) * (1 + ldl_int[2] / 100) - 1)
knitr::kable(tibble(
  Arm = c("Statin alone", "Evacetrapib 100 mg alone (AUC 5,900)", "Combination", "Independent-action prediction"),
  `LDL-C % change` = c(ldl_int, independent)
), digits = 1)
stopifnot(abs(ldl_int[1] - (-38.7)) < 1e-6, abs(ldl_int[3] - independent) < 0.5)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **EAUC50 covariate form (HDL-C).** Table 2 footnote f writes
  `EAUC50 = 5,380 * exp(0.00317 * (bHDL - 52.2))`. The authors' NONMEM code
  estimates the logarithm of EAUC50 and applies the baseline-HDL-C factor to
  that logarithm, `log(EAUC50) = 8.59 * exp(0.00317 * (bHDL - 52.2))`. The
  code's form is used: it reproduces Figure 2 (130% and 98% at 35 and 65 mg/dL)
  and the Discussion's 110% to 127% example, whereas the footnote's form
  gives about 115% and 111% at 35 and 65 mg/dL and 112% for the example.
- **Centring values.** Table 3 footnote e prints the LDL-C and triglyceride
  centring values rounded to 147 and 120 mg/dL; the NONMEM code uses 146.56
  and 120.01, which are used here.
- **Missing-covariate guards.** The authors' LDL-C code skips a covariate term
  when the baseline value is coded 0 (missing). The packaged model has no such
  guard: supply every baseline covariate.
- **Statin arm indicators.** The paper's indicators I_ST (statin alone) and
  I_COMB (statin with evacetrapib) are derived from `CONMED_STATIN` and
  `AUC_EVACETRAPIB > 0`. The HDL-C model's statin effect is held at 0 in the
  final model; its `CONMED_STATIN` column is kept only so the model matches the
  authors' code.
- **CL/F by dose.** The CL/F values quoted for 30, 100 and 500 mg in the
  Results are group summaries of individual estimates; the Table 1 equation
  is used as published, and the simulated 30 mg AUC is about 15-20% below the
  published geometric mean.
- **Patient count.** The PK text reports 226 patients; the NONMEM output
  reports 233 patients in the data file. The text value is recorded in the
  model metadata.
- **Virtual covariates.** CGCL, baseline HDL-C, LDL-C, triglycerides and ApoA1
  distributions, and their independence, are assumptions; the paper gives
  medians and means only.
- **Time origin.** `time` in the HDL-C model is the time from the first dose of
  study treatment in hours; the model describes the on-treatment period only
  (the paper's Figure 1 washout visit is not modelled).
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (EuropePMC
  search, 2026-11-20).
